list.atom: 16x8 register-backed FIFO with registered pop responses

global placement fills 60% of the core area, leaving room for the hold repair buffers and the clock tree that the resizers and CTS add after it; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

post placement hold repair targets 0.1 ns of slack instead of zero, so hold is still met once CTS and routing replace the placement estimates; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

post global route hold repair targets 0.05 ns; lower than the placement margin because routing estimates are in hand by then and the buffers cost area; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
lint with the PDK cell models in scope, so a standard cell the netlist instantiates is not reported as an undefined module; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

off: the XOR compares the Magic and KLayout GDS streams for tool disagreement, which is not a rule check and is not what TT precheck repeats; set it to 1 to have the flow catch a streamer disagreement itself; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

off: TT precheck runs the same KLayout decks over the submitted GDS after the flow (478.64s, zero items on 2026-09-18), so in flow DRC buys about eight minutes of duplicate coverage; the cost is that LibreLane records no klayout__drc_error__count, so collect reports no KLayout metric; set it to 1 when signoff has to be self contained; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

design repair does not put a buffer on every top level output; on a fixed TT tile those buffers spend core area on a load OUTPUT_CAP_LOAD already states to timing analysis; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
core area is inset from the top die edge by one standard cell row height; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
core area is inset from the bottom die edge by one standard cell row height; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

core area is inset from the left die edge by six site widths; wider than the vertical insets, keeping the cell rows clear of the tile boundary it abuts; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
core area is inset from the right die edge by six site widths, matching the left inset so the core stays centred in the tile; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

global routing reports congestion instead of failing the run; the die is fixed by the TT tile, so there is no floorplan to grow in response, and detailed routing is what decides whether the congestion was real; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
horizontal I/O pin shapes reach 2 um into the core, far enough for the router to land on a pin placed by the tile's DEF template; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

vertical I/O pin shapes reach 2 um into the core; the TT block DEF places this tile's signal pins on its top edge, so this is the one that carries them; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
vertical power straps every 50 um; with FP_PDN_VWIDTH this is how much routing resource the power grid takes out of the tile; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
vertical power straps are 2.1 um wide, the width the TT tile's power grid is cut for at the 50 um pitch above; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

run clock tree synthesis; this is LibreLane's own default, stated explicitly so a change to that default cannot silently leave the design on the ideal clock net synthesis assumed; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
single layer power distribution; a multilayer PDN puts straps on TopMetal1, which TT precheck forbids inside a tile; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

Magic streams the GDS without copying the DEF's labels into it; the tile's pins travel in the LEF that MAGIC_WRITE_LEF_PINONLY produces, not as GDS text; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430

Magic writes a pin only LEF for the tile, with no internal obstructions; that is the abstract the TT top level abuts, and it describes the tile as its pins; ttihp-verilog-template b86a2a781484bcab7ba522dc5de540086695a430
